question.problem: Find the surface area of the part of the surface $y=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}$ whose projection onto the $xz$-plane  is bounded by the constraints $-1\le x\le 1$ and $1\le z\le 2.$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $y=f(x,z)$ with $(x,z)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂y}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂y}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
y=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}},\,(x,z)\in D,
$$

where 

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,1\le z\le 2\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274587/assets/06abf7781e46ea3d3434ee26c6711cea2930fa8f73d534d6622931bf3c47c6a6.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂y}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}})=\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}})=\frac{z}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}},\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂y}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂y}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}})}^{2}+{(\frac{z}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{\frac{2({x}^{2}+{z}^{2})}{{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{2}{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot (1-(-1))\cdot (2-1) \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
